messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — planning a dry-run publish for Python + TS tonight 22:00 UTC. Need a quick confirmation on signing creds and dist-tag fallback behavior before we kick off. cc @sam @irene
deploy-bot: Scheduled dry-run: 2025-06-18T22:00:00Z for packages: @redwood/sdk-python @redwood/sdk-ts (:dry_run)
sam: I can check the signing keys now. Which KMS key are we using for the dry-run?
irene: FYI one of the service account tokens for the publish pipeline rotates tomorrow morning. If the dry-run starts tonight we should use the secondary key alias to avoid failures.
maya: Good catch. @sam can you verify the secondary alias maps to the signing key used by release pipeline? If yes we should note it in the run notes.
sam: Confirmed — secondary alias present and has Encrypt/Sign permissions. I pushed a short runbook note -> `infra/release/notes.md` (line: sign-key: alias/redwood-release-secondary).
ben: Also, request: for this dry-run let's exercise the dist-tag fallback path. We had an edgecase where `dist-tag` write failed and the publish left packages under `latest` only. Plan: after dry-run, attempt to set `canary-edge` tag then intentionally simulate a tag-write transient error to validate rollback. :eyes:
maya: That test sounds valuable but let's make sure it runs in a sandboxed cohort (no prod npm/org). Use the `redwood-sandbox` npm org and `pypi-test` index.
deploy-bot: Running step: `npm publish --tag canary-edge --registry https://npm.redwood-sandbox.test`
release-engineer: If tag-write fails, the pipeline should attempt 3 retries and then create a rollback job to remove the published artifact and emit an incident note. That's the desired behavior we want to validate.
ben: Can we also confirm examples/docs pin behavior? Somebody reported that examples still reference `@redwood/sdk@^1.2.0` which would pick up canary if we tag incorrectly.
docs: I can patch the example snippets to pin to `~1.2.0` for the dry-run docs, then revert after. Will open a tiny PR and link it here.
irene: About the signing fallback: if KMS is unavailable pipeline will try ephemeral GPG key stored in the CI vault. Need an explicit approve for that contingency — otherwise pipeline will fail fast (we want fail fast for dry-run).
maya: For dry-run let's keep fail-fast on signing (no ephemeral fallback). We want to observe the failure mode. OK to have ephemeral fallback enabled for prod publishes only.
sam: Noted. I'll flip the `USE_EPHEMERAL_SIGNING` flag to `false` in `ci/publish.env` for tonight.
deploy-bot: CI job queued: `release/dry-run/1745501234` -> job id 4481. Logs streaming: https://ci.redwood/reports/4481
ben: One more check: make sure dist-tag write errors are surfaced in the console log with `TAG_WRITE_FAILURE` code so ops can trigger the rollback playbook quickly.
release-engineer: Adding rollback trigger note: `if TAG_WRITE_FAILURE and retries exhausted => invoke rollback-job --artifact $PKG --reason tag_write`
docs: PR opened: https://git.redwood/p/redwood/docs/pulls/912 (adds pinned examples + note about dry-run sandbox)
maya: sweet. timeline: dry-run at 22:00 UTC, smoke-checks at +5m, tagging-failure simulation at +10m, rollback verification at +15m. If all green we merge doc PR and schedule final publish cut for next week.
sam: I'll be on call during window and will watch signing steps. Ping me if deploy-bot reports `SIGNING_ERROR`.
irene: I'll monitor the CI tokens and rotate if anything odd.
deploy-bot: Job 4481 started (dry-run). Current step: prepare-artifact -> OK
ben: Good luck team — ping me if you want me to trigger the simulated tag error manually. :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks all. Post results here after the run and attach the small checklist (signing, dist-tag, examples pin).
release-engineer: If we see silent partial publishes we escalate immediately. Otherwise proceed with normal post-dry-run cleanup and mark as `dry-run:success` or `dry-run:failure`.
deploy-bot: Job 4481 step: publish -> WARNING: TAG_WRITE_RETRY 1/3
sam: Seeing TAG_WRITE_RETRY. I'm watching logs -> looks like transient 504 from registry.
irene: Confirming CI token refresh happened at 22:02:14, no auth errors.
ben: If it ultimately fails, run the removal: `npm unpublish --force @redwood/sdk-ts@0.0.0-canary --registry https://npm.redwood-sandbox.test` and the equivalent `twine` delete from `pypi-test` if necessary.
maya: Copy that. Please paste the exact unpublish commands in the postmortem if we hit rollback.
docs: Will update the doc PR with a short rollback snippet.
release-engineer: Final: keep the `USE_EPHEMERAL_SIGNING=false` for this run. After run we revert to default.
deploy-bot: Job 4481 completed: dry-run finished. Result: PARTIAL_PUBLISH_DETECTED (1 package published without dist-tag).
maya: Uh ok — partial publish detected. Ben please run the removal steps and confirm.
ben: Running unpublish now. Command: `npm unpublish --force @redwood/sdk-ts@0.0.0-canary --registry https://npm.redwood-sandbox.test` -> success. twine delete for python dry-run package also executed -> success.
release-engineer: Marking this a successful dry-run: rollback behaved as expected. We'll update the runbook with the exact commands and tweak the pipeline to surface `PARTIAL_PUBLISH` as a distinct alert.
docs: Merged the pinned-example PR and added a short note about dry-run sandbox and rollback commands. PR merged -> https://git.redwood/p/redwood/docs/pulls/912
maya: Great work. Follow-up actions: 1) add `TAG_WRITE_FAILURE` explicit metric 2) keep ephemeral signing disabled for dry-runs by default 3) add unpublish snippet to runbook 4) schedule final publish next Tue 14:00 UTC. I'll make a checklist and post it in #release-calendar.
sam: Ack. I'll revert `ci/publish.env` flag after this channel if needed.
irene: I'll add a short alert to the CI ops dashboard about token rotation window.
deploy-bot: Incident note: dry-run 1745501234 => PARTIAL_PUBLISH_DETECTED -> rollback executed.
maya: closing thread — thanks everyone :tada:
